workflow_type.workflow_name: Customer support ticket triage in Gmail/Slack with Shopify order lookup, carrier tracking verification, Known Issues lookup, and Tickets Log update

canonical_sop_steps.description: Open Gmail label 'Support/Incoming' and scan unread threads; read the customer's message body and any prior thread context.
Switch to Slack and read the latest top-level messages in #support-incoming; open threads where customers have replied.

Scan the message body for the order ID; copy a 10-digit number (sometimes prefixed '#ORB-'). If multiple numbers are present, copy each. If none are found, skim earlier thread messages or signature blocks.
Paste the order ID into the Shopify admin search; open the order page and review line items, fulfillment status, tracking number, refund history, and prior customer notes.

canonical_sop_steps.tool: Google Chrome (USPS / FedEx / UPS tracking page)
canonical_sop_steps.description: If the order has shipped, copy the tracking number from the Shopify admin and paste it into the carrier's public tracking page; read the latest scan and compare against the admin's recorded status.
Open the 'Known Issues' tab; scan the list of issue patterns to see if the current ticket matches a known pattern with a canned response template and a default escalation owner.

Compose a reply that acknowledges the customer's specific complaint, cites the current order status and last carrier scan, and proposes a concrete next action (refund, reship, escalate to carrier) with a timeline. For refunds and reships the worker first checks with a teammate or the finance/ops owner before committing. Send the reply on the same channel the ticket arrived on.
Append a new row with timestamp, channel, order_id, issue_type, action_taken, owner, and status. The worker first eyeballs the sheet to avoid logging the same ticket twice when a thread is revisited.

individual_sop_steps.description: Open the 'Support/Incoming' label; read the top unread thread, mostly 'where is my order' messages.
Copy the 10-digit order ID from the customer's message body (e.g. 4811230055).
Paste the order ID into Shopify admin search; open the order; note the fulfillment status and tracking number.
Paste the tracking number into the USPS public tracking page; read the latest scan and the predicted delivery date.
Reply on the existing thread with the current status, last scan location, and expected delivery date; include a sentence offering to escalate if no movement in 48h.
Append a row capturing the ticket: timestamp, gmail, order_id, 'where-is-my-order', 'replied with tracking', self, 'closed'.

sessions.workflow_session_human_readable_name: Slack ticket — admin vs. carrier disagreement

individual_sop_steps.description: Open a new message claiming the package was marked delivered but never arrived; note that the customer mentions order #ORB-3148290771.
Search the admin for the order; open the order page; copy the FedEx tracking number; note 'admin says: Out for Delivery'.
Open the FedEx public tracking page with the tracking number; observe 'Delivered — 2 days ago, left at front door' which contradicts the admin's 'Out for Delivery'.
Find the 'delivered-but-missing' pattern row; copy the canned response template and the escalate-to owner.
Before promising anything, ping the listed escalate-to owner to confirm a reship is OK; then reply in the thread acknowledging the contradiction, sharing the FedEx scan, and offering a free reship.
Append the row: timestamp, slack, order_id, 'delivered-but-missing', 'reship initiated, escalated to OWNER_NAME_A', 'open'.

sessions.workflow_session_human_readable_name: Ticket with no order ID — ask customer for it

individual_sop_steps.description: Open a new 'Support/Incoming' thread; read the customer's complaint about a wrong item received; note no order ID anywhere in the body or signature.
Skim earlier threads from this sender to see if a recent order ID has been mentioned; none found.
Reply asking the customer for the order number (mention '#ORB-' format) and a photo of the wrong item received.
Append the row: timestamp, gmail, '(none)', 'wrong-item-received', 'awaiting order ID from customer', 'pending'.

sessions.workflow_session_human_readable_name: Two order IDs in one ticket — duplicate charge complaint

individual_sop_steps.description: Read a complaint that the customer was charged twice for what they believe is one order; the body mentions two 10-digit order IDs (7813901744 and 7813901788).
Open the first order; note the line items, total, and payment status.
Open the second order; observe it contains the same line items, was placed 4 minutes after the first, and shows status 'Paid'.
Scan 'Known Issues' for 'duplicate order'; find the matching row pointing to the finance owner and a refund template.
Reply on the thread confirming the duplicate, promising a refund within 5 business days for the second order, and asking the customer to confirm before the refund is initiated.
Append the row: timestamp, gmail, '7813901744 + 7813901788', 'duplicate-charge', 'refund proposed, awaiting customer confirm', 'pending'.
